He previously played in the [[NBA]] for the [[Atlanta Hawks]][http://www.ramblinwreck.com/sports/m-baskbl/spec-rel/102507aaa.html Mario West Makes Hawks Roster] and [[New Jersey Nets]]. ==High school and college career== West was a Douglas County player of the year as a senior at [[Douglas County High School (Douglasville, Georgia)|Douglas County High School]]. He also earned honorable mention all-state honors after averaging 22 points and 10 rebounds per game. West was team captain as a junior and senior. West played college basketball for [[Georgia Tech Yellow Jackets men's basketball|Georgia Tech]]. He joined the Tech squad as a walk-on in the fall of 2002, redshirted in 2002–03, and earned a scholarship for the 2003–04 season. He played in 103 games, averaging 3.2 points over his career, and 4.9 over his last two seasons. West departed Georgia Tech 16th on the school's all-time list for steals despite averaging only 13.9 minutes per game in four years. He was voted team captain during the 2006–07 season. West won the 2007 NCAA State Farm Slam Dunk Contest held during the tournament's Final Four week.{{cite web|title=Mario West Captures Slam Dunk Contest|url=http://www.ramblinwreck.com/sports/m-baskbl/spec-rel/032707aaa.html|website=ramblinwreck.com|date=27 March 2007|publisher=Georgia Tech Athletic Association}} West received a Bachelor of Science degree in management from Georgia Tech on May 6, 2006, and continued his studies during his final college basketball season with courses in Economics. ==Professional career== West went undrafted in the [[2007 NBA draft]] but was quickly signed by the [[Atlanta Hawks]], a team he spent his first two seasons with. West spent the first half of the 2009–10 season playing in the [[NBA Development League]] for the [[Maine Red Claws]], before re-joining the Hawks in January 2010. He remained with the Hawks for the rest of the season, and in 156 games for the team over three seasons, he averaged 0.8 points in 4.4 minutes per game. West was known as a hard worker and an intense defender. Atlanta Hawks Head Coach [[Mike Woodson]] was quoted as saying "I've been around this league a long time and I don't think I've ever seen a guy play as hard as Mario plays. He pushes guys in practice to play hard and if you don't play hard he embarrasses you in terms of just knocking the hell out of you." Teammate [[Acie Law]] said "You can ask anybody in this locker room, Mario's the hardest worker on the team. You have to be at practice to see him. His motor never stops."{{cite web|last1=Cooper|first1=Jon|title=Mario West Feature Story: Super Mario|url=http://www.nba.com/hawks/feature/Mario_West_Feature_112607.html|website=nba.com|publisher=Atlanta Hawks official site|accessdate=29 May 2017}} West re-joined the Maine Red Claws for the 2010–11 season, later signing with the [[New Jersey Nets]] in March 2011.[http://usatoday30.usatoday.com/sports/basketball/nba/2011-03-31-2172590623_x.htm Nets shake things up by signing West, waiving Ross][http://www.nba.com/2011/news/04/10/nets-west.ap/index.html Nets sign Mario West for rest of season] {{webarchive|url=https://web.archive.org/web/20110414130934/http://www.nba.com/2011/news/04/10/nets-west.ap/index.html |date=2011-04-14 }} He appeared in six games for the Nets to complete the 2010–11 season, averaging 3.7 points, 1.8 rebounds, 1.7 assists and 1.2 steals in 19.3 minutes per game.[https://www.basketball-reference.com/players/w/westma02.html Mario West NBA Stats] In June 2011, West joined [[Soles de Santo Domingo Este|Cocolos de San Pedro de Macorís]] of the [[Liga Nacional de Baloncesto]].[http://www.basketdominicano.info/2011/06/lnb-cocolos-anuncian-mario-west-como.html LNB: COCOLOS ANUNCIAN MARIO WEST COMO REFUERZO] {{in lang|es}} His stint lasted until early August.[http://listindiario.com/el-deporte/2011/8/9/199006/Basden-y-West-guian-a-Cocolos-sobre-los-Reales Basden y West guían a Cocolos sobre los Reales] {{Webarchive|url=https://web.archive.org/web/20160305094710/http://listindiario.com/el-deporte/2011/8/9/199006/Basden-y-West-guian-a-Cocolos-sobre-los-Reales |date=March 5, 2016 }} {{in lang|es}} On August 2, 2011, West signed with [[Tezenis Verona]] of Italy for the 2011–12 season.[http://www.sportando.com/en/italy/serie-a2-est/87813/tezenis-verona-tabs-nba-player-mario-west.html Tezenis Verona tabs NBA player Mario West] In June 2012, West moved to the Philippines where he joined the [[Meralco Bolts]].[http://www.sportando.com/en/world/asia/92275/meralco-bolts-land-former-nba-player-mario-west.html Meralco Bolts land former NBA player Mario West] In September 2012, he joined [[Cañeros del Este]] and helped them win the league championship while garnering Finals MVP honors in early October.[http://tataojordan.blogspot.com.au/2012/10/lnb-caneros-campeones-2012-mario-west_5.html LNB - CAÑEROS CAMPEONES 2012; MARIO WEST MVP] {{in lang|es}} Later that month, he joined La Villa for a short stint. In January 2013, West signed with [[Fuerza Regia]] of Mexico for the rest of the 2012–13 season. In June 2013, he re-joined the Meralco Bolts. He then returned to Fuerza Regia for the 2013–14 season. In March 2014, he moved to France and signed with [[SOMB Boulogne-sur-Mer|SO Maritime Boulogne]].[http://www.sportando.com/en/europe/france/113711/mario-west-inks-with-boulogne-sur-mer.html Mario West inks with Boulogne-sur-Mer] In May 2014, he returned the Meralco Bolts for a third stint.[http://www.sportando.com/en/world/asia/120592/meralco-bolts-sign-mario-west-to-replace-terrence-williams.html Meralco Bolts sign Mario West to replace Terrence Williams] In October 2014, West signed with [[Club La Unión|La Unión]] of Argentina for the 2014–15 season. He sustained an injury in February 2015 and was ruled out for the rest of the season. He remained in Argentina for the 2015–16 season, signing with [[Juventud Sionista]].[http://data.shamsports.com/content/pages/playerProfiles/profileDisplay.jsp?id=945 ShamSports.com: Mario West player profile] In May 2016, West returned to Georgia Tech in Atlanta when he was hired as the director of player personnel as part of head coach Josh Pastner's
